newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BOOSTS CONFIDENCE WITH "MIRACLE" WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BOOSTS CONFIDENCE WITH "MIRACLE" WIN.

text.p: Yevgeny Kafelnikov, who said it would take a miracle for him to retain his French Open crown, needed one on Friday to advance to the last 16 after an exhausting five-set battle with local favourite Cedric Pioline.
Russian Kafelnikov, the third seed, was 4-3 behind in the fifth set but still found the strength to recover and win 7-5 6-4 6-7 1-6 6-4.
"When I lost the third set, I thought I would never make it," said the 23-year-old from the Black Sea resort of Sochi.

The Russian was sidelined for over three months earlier in the season after breaking a finger in his right hand in January. "I haven't played for five sets for a long time and I felt exhausted. In a way, it is a miracle."

Kafelnikov, who ruled himself out as a contender before the tournament started, had not dropped a set in his first two matches and the kind of test he underwent against Pioline was probably just what he needed to boost his confidence.

"My physical condition is still not quite what it used to be but it's improving and so is my game," he said. "I'm not saying I'm going to win here but it's true that I'm more confident than I was a few days ago."
Kafelnikov made a good start, using his trademark, powerful ground strokes and a few astute drop-shots to win the first two sets.

But Pioline, cheered on by a partisan crowd at centre court on a beautiful afternoon, used a tie-break to win a tense third set and took advantage of a tiring Kafelnikov to take the fourth 6-1 in just 26 minutes.
The Frenchman, once a top 10 player but now 33rd in the world rankings, moved closer to victory by breaking his opponent to lead 4-3 in the last set.
But he lost the following game, double-faulting on break point and Kafelnikov then took the next two games with Pioline hitting a backhand long on match point.

"It's only when I broke back in the last set that I realised I had a chance of winning," said Kafelnikov. "Pioline played well and came close. He probably knew that I was not quite as good as last year and thought he could beat me."
Kafelnikov said he was surprised that people were paying little attention to him.

"It's funny, they keep asking me for my badge when I walk in the alleys," he said. "I'm the champion and they still want to see my badge. It's the same with the crowd, they always seem to support the other guy."
The Russian faces hard-hitting Australian Mark Philippoussis in the next round for what should be an exciting clash of styles.
"He's powerful and playing well at the moment," said Kafelnikov. "I don't think I'll win but after all, I'm the champion, I'm good on clay and there might be another miracle."
